device_message_id.description: Sender-assigned stable identity of one logical to-device message. Queue services MUST preserve it byte-for-byte across retries and redelivery. Receivers deduplicate by (sender_principal_id, sender endpoint id, device_message_id), where the endpoint id is sender_device_id, sender_agent_id, or sender_id according to the closed sender branch.

sender_principal_id.description: Sender Principal DID. Intentionally NOT named sender_actor_id: device messages are out-of-band per-device transport envelopes that travel principal-to-principal outside any Realm context, so the Realm-scoped Actor identity used by message.schema.json / event-payload.schema.json does not apply here. For a device sender, pair it with sender_device_id and verify that pair against the accepted PCR device projection; for a Native Agent sender it equals sender_agent_id and the signer is anchored by sender_agent_verification_method plus sender_agent_key_authorize_event_id. For the restricted Principal Server service branch it MUST equal recipient_principal_id: the holder remains the message principal while sender_id identifies the internal materializer.

sender_device_id.description: Authoring human device. Exactly one sender endpoint branch is present: this field, the complete sender_agent_* triple, or sender_id. A Native Agent runtime has no device identity and MUST NOT be disguised as an ak:device (crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 9.0.1); the restricted Principal Server materializer likewise has a service identity rather than a fake device. Receivers use the selected endpoint field in the device-message deduplication key.

sender_agent_id.description: Native Agent principal that authored this message. Present exactly when the sender is an Agent runtime, together with sender_agent_verification_method and sender_agent_key_authorize_event_id. It equals sender_principal_id; carrying it explicitly is what makes the endpoint branch decidable from the envelope alone, matching the consume / claim_envelope XORs of crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 9.0.1.

sender_agent_verification_method.description: Verification method the Agent currently signs with. The device branch gets the equivalent from the accepted device projection; without this the receiver would hold an Agent principal id and no way to say which key speaks for it.

sender_agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted Agent key authorization Event that anchors sender_agent_verification_method.

sender_id.description: Principal Server service identity that internally materialized an actor-private update for the holder. This branch is restricted to actor_private_update_kind, sender_principal_id MUST equal recipient_principal_id, and the service id MUST equal the Principal Server identity bound to the recipient's current authenticated self/to-device surface. It is not a bearer delegation and cannot be submitted through ak.self.device_messages.command.send.v1.

recipient_principal_id.description: Recipient Principal DID. Same naming rationale as sender_principal_id — device messages are not Realm-scoped, so Actor identity is not used. Pair with recipient_device_id for targeted device delivery.

unsigned.description: Optional non-authenticated metadata block (transport-layer hints only). Receivers MUST NOT trust any field here for authorization, ordering, or cryptographic verification. Typical sub-fields: progress (delivery progress hint), error_context (transport-layer error diagnostics), retry_after_ms. By convention this block is excluded from the signed transcript of the enclosing transport envelope and is dropped on persist.

allOf.$comment: Closed sender endpoint XOR: sender_device_id alone, the complete sender_agent_* triple alone, or sender_id alone. Half-filled and mixed branches are rejected.

Only the recipient Principal Server's internal materializer may use the service branch, and only for the closed actor-private update kind set. Principal equality and authenticated service binding are semantic checks described by the normative prose.

actor_private_update_kind.description: Closed DeviceMessageEnvelope.kind set for actor-private sibling-device projection updates. These values are transport discriminators, not Event kinds and never enter shared Realm history.

secret_request_content.description: ak.secret.request to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §10.7). A newly authorized device asks an existing authorized device to hand over an account-scope secret over HPKE. Carries no secret material itself.

request_id.description: Caller-generated random correlation id; MUST NOT be reused after the request is answered or cancelled.

secret_id.description: Opaque identifier of the requested secret, e.g. example_mls_account_secret.

from_device_id.description: Requesting (new) device; MUST equal envelope sender_device_id.

recipient_hpke_public_key.description: base64url X25519 HPKE public key the requesting device controls and the responder seals to. It MUST be byte-identical to the hpke_key registered for from_device in the current accepted device projection. A responder MUST fail closed on any mismatch and MUST NOT accept an ephemeral key merely because it appeared in a bound SAS verification transcript; SAS authenticates device signing keys, not HPKE sealing keys.

secret_send_content.description: ak.secret.send to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §10.7). The existing authorized device returns the requested secret HPKE-sealed to the requester's recipient_hpke_public_key. The plaintext is never visible to the queue service.

request_id.description: Correlates to the pending ak.secret.request; MUST equal the request_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and HPKE AAD. Receivers MUST drop sends that do not match a locally pending request_id.

secret_id.description: Opaque requested secret identifier; MUST equal the secret_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and HPKE AAD.

from_device_id.description: Authorizing (existing) device; MUST equal envelope sender_device_id and MUST be a non-revoked device of the recipient principal.

ciphertext.description: base64url HPKE AEAD ciphertext over the secret plaintext. The plaintext MUST carry the requested secret body, version, request_id and secret_id. The HPKE AAD is the RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of {device_message_id, kind, sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, recipient_principal_id, recipient_device_id, request_id, secret_id, expires_at}; expires_at is the exact already-validated canonical Arkret UTC millisecond string from DeviceMessageEnvelope and MUST NOT be converted to a second epoch field. Freshness for server-assigned sent_at is bound by the sender-assigned device_message_id plus the one-time request_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and AAD.

purpose.description: Optional verification purpose. Omitted means generic device key verification. same_principal_device_authorization is used when a fresh device asks already authorized devices of the same principal to approve device authorization.

pairing_code.description: Eight-character human-readable Crockford-style device-pairing code bound into a same-principal authorization transcript. It is short-lived, one-time, and locked after ten failed submissions.

new_device_pubkey.description: Canonical PublicKey for the requesting device when purpose=same_principal_device_authorization. kid MUST be the requesting ak:device:<uuidv7> id and the key material MUST be carried in key. The {kid, alg, public_key} spelling is not canonical wire and MUST be rejected. The object is later consumed verbatim by ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.v1.

challenge_proof.description: Fresh requesting-device proof of possession over the ak.device-pairing.challenge.to_device.v1 transcript, which commits to {expires_at, gate_audience, new_device_pubkey_digest, pairing_code, request_canonical_digest, transaction_id}. The receiving authorized device MUST recompute the transcript from the values it displays to the user and verify the signature before treating the requesting device as pairable; it is later submitted verbatim to ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.v1.

target_attestation.description: Closed accepted_device possession attestation of the requesting device when purpose=same_principal_device_authorization, and the only authority for its hpke_key and algorithms. It is the same schema and same domain the short-link path uses, because it binds only pairing_challenge_transcript_digest and each path already closes its own challenge transcript. The receiving authorized device MUST rebuild and verify it after the challenge proof, requiring device_id to equal new_device_pubkey.kid, device_public_key_did to decode to the same key as new_device_pubkey.key, and pairing_challenge_transcript_digest to equal the transcript digest it just recomputed; only then may it read hpke_key and algorithms from it and copy device_signature verbatim into the ak.device.authorize payload. It travels only on this out-of-band message and MUST NOT be posted back through the unauthenticated stage or resolve surface.

gate_audience.description: Auth Server audience/origin expected to consume the paired proof.

request_canonical_digest.description: Digest of the canonical request material bound into the pairing proof.

device_metadata.description: User-facing requesting-device hints. Receivers MUST treat this as display metadata and bind the parts shown to the user into the verification transcript.
